add-214.title: Tamriya (Date Slice with Sesame and Tahini)
add-214.culturalNotes: Tamriya is served with Arabic coffee in the Gulf, and the slightly bitter tahini balances the sweetness of the dates.

instructions.1: Warm the dates with the butter over low heat, stirring and mashing until soft and smooth.
instructions.2: Add the biscuit crumbs, cardamom, cinnamon and half the sesame and knead well.
instructions.3: Press into a tray lined with baking paper 1.5 cm thick and level.
instructions.4: Spread the tahini over the top, sprinkle with the rest of the sesame, chill an hour and cut into squares.

add-215.title: Date and Nut Balls
add-215.culturalNotes: A healthy alternative to processed sweets and a quick energy source; you can press a whole almond into each ball.

add-215-i2.name: Baladi ghee, butter or coconut oil

instructions.1: If the dates are firm, warm them with the ghee over very low heat, stirring, until soft.
instructions.2: Mix the dates with the nuts, cinnamon and cardamom until evenly spread.
instructions.3: Roll into walnut-sized balls with ghee-greased hands.
instructions.4: Roll in coconut or sesame and keep in an airtight container.

add-216.title: Sudanese Helo-Mur (Abreh) Drink
add-216.prepTime: a week to sprout the sorghum
add-216.culturalNotes: Helo-mur is Sudan's most famous Ramadan drink, and making its flakes is a communal ritual weeks before the month. Ready-made flakes are sold in Sudanese shops, cutting the work to soaking.

add-216-i3.name: Helo-mur spices: cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, cloves, black cumin, fenugreek

add-216-i6.name: To serve: sugar and cold water

instructions.1: Zariaa: soak the sorghum a day, spread on a damp cloth and cover until it sprouts (5-7 days), then sun-dry and grind.
instructions.2: Mix the sprouted flour with the sorghum flour, ground spices and soaked dates, add water into a batter and leave two days to ferment.
instructions.3: Spread the mixture very thin on a hot griddle until dry, browned and crisp flakes form, then break and store them.
instructions.4: To serve: soak the flakes in cold water for 2-3 hours until their flavour and colour dissolve.
instructions.5: Strain, sweeten with sugar and serve ice-cold at iftar.

add-217.title: Dates with Milk (Balah bel Laban)
add-217.culturalNotes: Dates with milk is the Ramadan iftar drink in Egypt, giving quick energy after fasting. Soaking the dates first gives a velvety texture with no bits.

add-217-i4.name: Crushed nuts and coconut to garnish

instructions.1: Wash and pit the dates and soak in a cup of the milk for an hour until soft.
instructions.2: Blend the dates with the soaking milk until completely smooth, then add the rest of the milk and blend a minute.
instructions.3: Serve cold or warm with a sprinkle of nuts, or leave the dates in pieces in the milk without blending, as you prefer.

add-218.title: Creamy Cheddar Cheese Sauce
add-218.culturalNotes: Grating the cheddar yourself rather than using pre-grated makes it melt smoothly, since pre-grated contains anti-caking starch. Don't let the sauce boil after adding the cheese or it turns grainy.

instructions.1: Melt the butter, add the flour and stir a minute without colouring.
instructions.2: Whisk in the milk gradually so it doesn't lump, and cook until slightly thickened.
instructions.3: Lower the heat right down and add the cheddar in batches, stirring until completely melted, then the mustard and paprika.
instructions.4: Serve warm with nachos, fries and burgers, thinning with a little milk if it thickens.

add-219.title: Baked Potato Kibbeh Tray
add-219.culturalNotes: Potato kibbeh is an easier and cheaper version of traditional kibbeh, and the bulgur gives it the firmness and familiar kibbeh texture.

instructions.1: Knead the potato with the bulgur, egg and spices, adding flour if soft, until the dough holds together.
instructions.2: Soften the onion, then cook the meat with the spices, and add the pine nuts.
instructions.3: Spread half the potato dough in a greased tray, spread the filling, then cover with the rest of the dough and smooth with a wet hand.
instructions.4: Score the top in a crisscross with a knife and brush with ghee.
instructions.5: Bake at 200°C for 35-40 minutes until the top is golden and crisp.
instructions.6: Serve with yogurt and green salad.

add-220.title: Lebanese Bayaz (Onion, Parsley and Sumac Salad)
add-220.culturalNotes: Rubbing the onion with salt and sumac takes away its sharpness and makes it soft and tangy; it is the classic partner of grills in Lebanese restaurants.

instructions.1: Rub the sliced onion with the salt and sumac between your fingers for a minute until it softens and turns purple.
instructions.2: Add the parsley and toss.
instructions.3: Drizzle with olive oil and lemon if you like and serve at once with grills, kofta and shawarma.

add-221.title: Seasoned Baked Potato Wedges
add-221.culturalNotes: Soaking to remove starch, then drying well, is the secret of crisp oven wedges without frying.

instructions.1: Scrub the potatoes well, halve each lengthwise, then cut each half into 3-4 thick wedges.
instructions.2: Soak in cold water for 15 minutes to remove the starch, then dry completely.
instructions.3: Toss with the oil, spices and salt until coated.
instructions.4: Spread skin-side down on a lined tray and bake at 220°C for 30-35 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.
instructions.5: Sprinkle with Parmesan while hot and serve with garlic sauce or ketchup.

add-222.title: Cheesy Garlic Bread
add-222.culturalNotes: Wrapping the bread in foil first lets the garlic butter soak in, and opening it at the end gives the crunch.

add-222-i6.name: A pinch of salt and oregano

instructions.1: Mix the soft butter with the garlic, parsley, salt and oregano.
instructions.2: Slice the bread diagonally without cutting all the way through, or split lengthwise.
instructions.3: Spread the garlic butter inside the slices and top with the cheese.
instructions.4: Wrap in foil and bake at 200°C for 8 minutes, then open the foil and bake 3-4 minutes until the cheese melts and the bread crisps.
instructions.5: Serve hot with pasta or soup.

add-223.title: Slow-Simmered Bone Broth
add-223.culturalNotes: Vinegar helps extract minerals and collagen from the bones, and a successful broth turns to jelly when chilled.

add-223-i1.name: Beef, lamb or chicken bones (with marrow and joints)

add-223-i6.name: Garlic, bay leaf, peppercorns and cinnamon stick

add-223-i7.name: Water
add-223-i7.standardAmount: to cover the bones by 5 cm

instructions.1: Roast the bones at 220°C for 30 minutes until browned (optional, for a darker, richer broth).
instructions.2: Put the bones in a large pot, cover with water, add the vinegar and leave 30 minutes before heating.
instructions.3: Bring to the boil and skim the foam, then add the vegetables and spices.
instructions.4: Simmer on the lowest possible heat for 8-12 hours (4 hours for chicken), topping up with water if needed.
instructions.5: Strain, cool, skim the fat and keep in the fridge 5 days or freeze; salt when using.

add-224.title: Iced Mocha
add-224.culturalNotes: Mocha is a mix of coffee and chocolate. Freezing coffee into ice cubes instead of plain ice stops the drink from getting diluted.

instructions.1: Dissolve the coffee and sugar in the warm water and let cool slightly.
instructions.2: Drizzle lines of chocolate sauce inside the glass.
instructions.3: Whisk or blend the coffee with the milk and a spoon of chocolate sauce until frothy.
instructions.4: Fill the glass with ice, pour the mocha over and top with whipped cream and a sprinkle of cocoa.

add-225.title: Homemade Dessert Ashta (Clotted-Style Cream)
add-225.culturalNotes: A stable ashta that doesn't run in the oven or when cut, with little sugar because Middle Eastern sweets are soaked in syrup.

instructions.1: Dissolve the cornflour, cream powder and sugar in the cold milk, then stir constantly over medium heat until very thick.
instructions.2: Remove from the heat, add the orange-blossom water and let it cool to lukewarm, stirring now and then.
instructions.3: Add the canned cream and whisk until smooth and creamy.
instructions.4: Cover with cling film touching the surface and chill; use to fill qatayef, kunafa and basbousa and to decorate desserts.

add-226.title: Indian Chapati
add-226.culturalNotes: Chapati is an everyday bread in India, East Africa and Yemen. Rolling it with ghee then rolling out again gives soft layers.

instructions.1: Mix the flour, salt and oil, add the water gradually and knead into a smooth, soft dough; rest 20 minutes.
instructions.2: Divide into 10 balls, roll each into a thin round, brush with ghee, fold, coil into a spiral and roll out again (for layers).
instructions.3: Heat an iron or non-stick pan and cook each bread until bubbles appear, then flip, brush with ghee and press with a spatula until it puffs and spots golden.
instructions.4: Stack the breads under a cloth and serve with curry and masala.

add-227.title: Karak Chai
add-227.culturalNotes: Karak is the favourite street drink of the Gulf, originally from Indian chai. Letting it boil up several times gives its creamy body and concentrated flavour.

add-227-i2.name: Loose black tea or tea granules

instructions.1: Boil the water with the cardamom, cloves and cinnamon for 3 minutes.
instructions.2: Add the tea and sugar and simmer on low heat for 5-7 minutes until strong and dark.
instructions.3: Add the evaporated milk and saffron and let it rise, then lower the heat and let it rise two or three more times.
instructions.4: Strain and serve hot in small cups.

add-228.title: Egyptian Savory Qaraqeesh (Salted Eid Kaak)
add-228.culturalNotes: Savory qaraqeesh are baked alongside Eid kahk in Egypt and served with tea; fennel and anise give them their distinctive aroma.

instructions.1: Rub the flour with the ghee until fully absorbed.
instructions.2: Add the yeast, sesame, fennel, anise, nigella, sugar and salt, then the warm water gradually, and bring together lightly.
instructions.3: Cover and rest 30-45 minutes until doubled.
instructions.4: Roll part of the dough into a long strip and cut diagonally into fingers, or shape small rings; arrange on trays and rest 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C until the bases colour, then turn on the grill to lightly brown the tops.
instructions.6: Let cool completely to crisp up and store in airtight tins.

add-229.title: Crispy Orange Cookies
add-229.culturalNotes: Economical Eid cookies; the zest carries more flavour than the juice because the aromatic oils are in the peel.

add-229-i8.name: Vanilla and a pinch of salt

instructions.1: Cream the butter with the icing sugar and zest, then add the eggs and vanilla.
instructions.2: Add the flour, baking powder and salt alternately with the orange juice into a smooth dough.
instructions.3: Shape with a cookie press or piping bag, or roll and cut with cutters, onto lined trays.
instructions.4: Bake at 180°C for 12-15 minutes until the edges colour.
instructions.5: Let cool completely to crisp and store in airtight tins.

add-230.title: Hijazi Almond 'Coffee' (Milk and Almond Drink)
add-230.culturalNotes: Almond 'coffee' is a winter drink from the Hijaz, called coffee although it contains none. It is served to guests on cold winter nights.

instructions.1: Blanch the almonds for 2 minutes, peel and crush coarsely.
instructions.2: Dissolve the rice flour and sugar in the cold milk, then heat over medium heat, stirring constantly.
instructions.3: Add the almonds and cardamom and simmer on low heat 10 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened.
instructions.4: Add the saffron or rose water and serve hot in cups with almond pieces.

add-231.title: Three-Cheese Mint Samosa
add-231.culturalNotes: Feta gives saltiness, mozzarella the stretch and cheddar a strong flavour, while mint adds freshness to balance the richness.

add-231-i1.name: Feta or salty white cheese, crumbled

add-231-i4.name: Dried mint (or ½ cup fresh, chopped)

add-231-i8.name: Flour and water paste to seal

instructions.1: Mix the three cheeses with the mint, nigella seeds and egg until combined.
instructions.2: Put a spoonful of filling on the edge of each sheet and fold into successive triangles to the end.
instructions.3: Seal the end with the flour paste.
instructions.4: Fry in hot oil until golden on both sides and drain on kitchen paper.
instructions.5: Serve hot with the cheese stretchy.

add-232.title: Chicken, Corn and Mayo Samosa
add-232.culturalNotes: A creative filling children love; samosas can be made and frozen before frying for the Ramadan table.

add-232-i1.name: Boiled chicken breast, finely chopped or shredded

add-232-i6.name: Garlic powder, paprika, salt and black pepper

instructions.1: Mix the chicken with the corn, mayonnaise, cheese, parsley and spices into a creamy filling that holds together.
instructions.2: Fill the sheets and fold into triangles, sealing the end with a flour-and-water paste.
instructions.3: Fry in hot oil until golden, or brush with oil and bake at 200°C for 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Serve hot with sweet chilli sauce.

add-233.title: Classic French Chocolate Mousse
add-233.culturalNotes: Classic French mousse uses raw eggs, so use very fresh or pasteurised eggs. Folding gently keeps it light.

add-233-i2.name: Large eggs, separated, at room temperature

add-233-i6.name: Chocolate shavings or berries to decorate

instructions.1: Melt the chocolate over a water bath and let it cool to lukewarm.
instructions.2: Stir the yolks one at a time into the lukewarm chocolate, then the vanilla.
instructions.3: Whip the cream to soft peaks, and whisk the whites with the icing sugar until firm.
instructions.4: Fold the cream into the chocolate gently, then the whites in two additions with a folding motion so the air isn't lost.
instructions.5: Divide into glasses and chill at least 4 hours; decorate before serving.

add-234.title: Fresh Mango Juice
add-234.culturalNotes: Very ripe mangoes provide most of the sweetness. The best varieties for juice are Owais, Zebdia and Fass.

instructions.1: Peel the mangoes and cut the flesh away from the stone.
instructions.2: Blend with the water, sugar and lemon until completely smooth.
instructions.3: Strain if you prefer a light juice and serve chilled at once.
instructions.4: For mango with milk, use cold milk instead of water and add a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

add-235.title: Watermelon Mint Juice
add-235.culturalNotes: Watermelon needs no water because it is almost all water. Freezing watermelon cubes to use instead of ice keeps the flavour concentrated.

instructions.1: Cut the watermelon into cubes and remove the seeds.
instructions.2: Blend with the lemon, mint and sugar for a few seconds until liquid.
instructions.3: Strain if you like and serve at once over ice.

add-236.title: Classic Vanilla Custard
add-236.culturalNotes: Pouring the hot milk onto the yolks gradually (tempering) stops the eggs curdling. Homemade custard with yolks is far richer than custard powder.

instructions.1: Heat the milk until almost boiling.
instructions.2: Whisk the yolks with the sugar and cornflour until pale and smooth.
instructions.3: Pour a third of the hot milk gradually onto the yolks, whisking, then return the mixture to the pan.
instructions.4: Stir constantly over medium heat until thick and boiling for a minute, then remove and add the vanilla and butter.
instructions.5: Pour into serving dishes, cover with cling film touching the surface so no skin forms, chill and serve with fruit.

add-237.title: Stovetop Popcorn
add-237.culturalNotes: Leaving a gap for steam makes the popcorn crisp rather than chewy, and removing it as soon as the popping slows stops the bottom burning.

add-237-i5.name: Extras: cheese powder, caramel or paprika

instructions.1: Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pot over medium-high heat with 3 test kernels.
instructions.2: When the three pop, add the rest of the kernels, cover leaving a small gap for steam, and shake the pot now and then.
instructions.3: When the popping slows to two seconds between pops, take the pot off the heat at once.
instructions.4: Tip the popcorn into a large bowl and toss with the salt, butter and extras.

add-238.title: Grilled Corn on the Cob
add-238.culturalNotes: Charcoal-grilled corn is the classic summer snack of the Nile Corniche and Alexandria. Rubbing the cob with a lemon slice dipped in salt and chilli is a popular touch.

instructions.1: Remove the husks and silk, and boil the cobs 5 minutes beforehand if you want to shorten the grilling.
instructions.2: Grill over charcoal, a direct gas flame or a hot grill, turning constantly, until the kernels brown with a few black spots, 10-15 minutes.
instructions.3: Brush with butter while hot, sprinkle with salt, squeeze over lemon and add a pinch of chilli.

add-239.title: Chicken and Vegetable Crêpes
add-239.culturalNotes: Resting the batter before cooking makes the crêpes softer and less likely to tear. Crêpes can be made ahead and frozen between sheets of baking paper.

add-239-i11.name: White sauce or mayonnaise and mustard

add-239-i12.name: Paprika, garlic powder and black pepper

instructions.1: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, salt and oil into a smooth, lump-free batter and rest 15 minutes.
instructions.2: Heat a lightly greased non-stick pan, pour in a ladleful and swirl to cover the base, cooking a minute each side.
instructions.3: Sauté the onion, peppers and mushrooms, add the chicken and spices, then the sauce, and stir.
instructions.4: Put the filling in the middle of each crêpe, sprinkle with cheese and fold into a roll or triangle.
instructions.5: Return to the pan or oven for a few minutes until the cheese melts.
instructions.6: Serve hot with cheese sauce or ketchup.

add-240.title: Molten Chocolate Lava Cake
add-240.culturalNotes: A hot oven and short time are the secret: the crust sets and the centre stays molten. The ramekins can be filled and chilled until baking, adding two minutes.

add-240-i7.name: A pinch of salt and vanilla

add-240-i8.name: Cocoa and butter for the moulds

instructions.1: Butter 4 ramekins and dust with cocoa.
instructions.2: Melt the chocolate with the butter over a water bath until smooth.
instructions.3: Whisk the eggs, yolks and sugar until pale, add the melted chocolate, then fold in the flour, salt and vanilla gently.
instructions.4: Divide among the ramekins and bake in an oven preheated to 220°C for 10-12 minutes until the edges set and the centre still wobbles.
instructions.5: Leave just one minute, then turn out onto a plate and serve at once with ice cream.

add-241.title: Buttered Corn Cups
add-241.culturalNotes: A light street snack loved by children; frozen corn gives excellent results all year.

add-241-i4.name: Extras: grated cheese, mayonnaise, paprika, chilli, lemon

instructions.1: Boil the corn in salted water for 5 minutes or heat in the microwave, then drain.
instructions.2: Toss with the butter and salt over the heat for a minute until coated.
instructions.3: Divide into cups and add the extras you like (Mexican street style: mayonnaise, cheese, paprika and lemon).

add-242.title: Homemade Shanklish Cheese
add-242.culturalNotes: Traditional shanklish is aged for weeks until a beneficial mould forms; this is a quick, milder home version eaten after a few days.

instructions.1: Strain the yogurt in a clean cloth hung over a bowl in the fridge for 24 hours until it becomes very dry labneh.
instructions.2: Mix with the salt, chilli and spices.
instructions.3: Shape into balls the size of a small orange with oiled hands.
instructions.4: Arrange on a tray lined with baking paper in a dry, cool, airy place for 3-4 days until the outside dries.
instructions.5: Roll the balls in dried thyme or chilli and keep in a jar covered with olive oil or in the fridge.

add-243.title: Mint Yogurt Sauce
add-243.culturalNotes: A refreshing Indian-style sauce; the little sugar balances the heat of the chilli and lemon. Without yogurt it becomes a green chutney that keeps longer.

instructions.1: Grind the mint, coriander, garlic, chilli, lemon, sugar and salt in a processor into a paste.
instructions.2: Add the olive oil gradually with the processor running.
instructions.3: Mix the paste with the yogurt and serve cold with grills, samosa and pakora; keeps two days in the fridge.

add-244.title: Fruit and Avocado Salad
add-244.culturalNotes: Avocado adds a creamy texture and healthy fats that make the salad more filling; it goes in last so it isn't mashed.

instructions.1: Cube the avocado and sprinkle at once with lemon juice so it doesn't brown.
instructions.2: Cut the rest of the fruit and toss gently with the avocado in a bowl.
instructions.3: Mix the honey with the orange and lemon juice.
instructions.4: Pour the dressing over the fruit, sprinkle with mint and serve cold at once.

add-245.title: Cream of Mushroom Soup
add-245.culturalNotes: Browning the mushrooms until their water evaporates before adding stock gives the soup a deep flavour instead of a boiled-mushroom taste.

instructions.1: Soften the onion in the butter, then the garlic for a minute.
instructions.2: Add the mushrooms and stir on high heat until they release their water, it evaporates and they brown slightly; set a handful aside to garnish.
instructions.3: Sprinkle in the flour and stir a minute, then add the stock gradually and the thyme and simmer 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Blend the soup smooth with a stick blender, or leave it chunky.
instructions.5: Add the cream, nutmeg, salt and pepper, heat without boiling and serve garnished with the browned mushrooms and parsley.

add-246.title: Egyptian-Style Everyday Pasta with Meat Sauce
add-246.culturalNotes: Everyday pasta is the quick weeknight meal of the Egyptian home. The pasta water binds the sauce to the pasta and makes it glossy.

add-246-i8.name: Mixed spice, black pepper and salt

instructions.1: Boil the pasta in salted water until cooked and drain, keeping a cup of the cooking water.
instructions.2: Soften the onion, then cook the meat, garlic and spices until done.
instructions.3: Add the tomato paste, then the tomato juice, and simmer 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Toss the pasta in the sauce with a little of the cooking water and serve sprinkled with roumi cheese.

add-247.title: Soft Homemade Burger Buns
add-247.culturalNotes: Milk, butter and egg give burger buns their familiar softness, and shaping tight balls makes them rise evenly.

instructions.1: Knead the flour, yeast, sugar and salt with the milk and egg, then add the butter and knead 10 minutes until smooth and glossy.
instructions.2: Cover and leave an hour until doubled.
instructions.3: Divide into 8 equal pieces, shape into tight balls, arrange on a lined tray and press lightly.
instructions.4: Leave 45 minutes until puffed, brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with sesame.
instructions.5: Bake at 190°C for 15 minutes until golden.
instructions.6: Cover with a cloth as soon as they come out so they stay soft.

add-248.title: Berry Yogurt Smoothie
add-248.culturalNotes: Yogurt adds protein and good bacteria, and oats make it a filling breakfast.

instructions.1: Put the milk and yogurt in the blender first, then the berries, honey and oats.
instructions.2: Blend until smooth and thick and serve at once.

add-249.title: Egyptian Fino (Samoli) Bread Rolls
add-249.culturalNotes: Fino is Egypt's favourite sandwich bread. Steam in the oven gives it a thin, glossy, crisp crust.

instructions.1: Mix the flour, salt, sugar and yeast, add the warm water and knead, then add the oil and knead 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
instructions.2: Cover and leave an hour until doubled.
instructions.3: Divide into 8 pieces, roll each into a rectangle, then roll up tightly and shape into a long roll with tapered ends.
instructions.4: Arrange on a tray and leave 45 minutes until puffed, then slash lengthwise with a sharp blade.
instructions.5: Bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes with a tray of water at the bottom of the oven for steam, until golden.
instructions.6: Cool on a rack.

add-250.title: Banana Peanut Butter Smoothie
add-250.culturalNotes: A protein- and energy-rich smoothie, good after exercise or as a quick breakfast.

instructions.1: Put the milk in the blender first, then the banana, peanut butter, honey and extras.
instructions.2: Blend until smooth and thick and serve at once with a pinch of cinnamon.

add-251.title: Breaded Fried Liver
add-251.culturalNotes: Liver toughens if overcooked or salted too early, so fry it quickly over high heat to keep it tender inside.

instructions.1: Pound the liver slices gently to make them thin and even and remove the membranes.
instructions.2: Marinate with the garlic, lemon, cumin and pepper for 30 minutes, adding the salt just before coating.
instructions.3: Coat each slice in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
instructions.4: Fry in hot oil for 1½-2 minutes per side until just golden.
instructions.5: Drain and serve at once with lemon, tahini and fries.

add-252.title: Spiced Sausage (Sujuk) Skillet
add-252.culturalNotes: Oriental sausage (Alexandrian sausage or maqaniq) cooks in its own fat, so little oil is needed. Pomegranate molasses gives a tangy Levantine taste.

instructions.1: Cut the sausage into pieces or rings.
instructions.2: Brown the sausage in the oil until coloured and releasing its fat, then lift out.
instructions.3: Soften the onion, garlic and peppers in the same oil.
instructions.4: Add the tomatoes and spices and stir until soft, then return the sausage and toss with the pomegranate molasses for 2 minutes.
instructions.5: Serve hot in bread or with fried eggs.

add-253.title: Spicy Egyptian Feshah (Sautéed Lungs)
add-253.culturalNotes: Feshah is a popular Eid al-Adha dish in Egypt; boiling it well first with vinegar and spices removes its smell and tenderises it.

add-253-i2.name: For boiling: onion, bay leaves, cardamom and vinegar

add-253-i7.name: Cumin, chilli, mixed spice and black pepper

instructions.1: Wash the lungs well with water and vinegar and cut into large pieces.
instructions.2: Boil with the onion, bay leaves and cardamom for 45 minutes until cooked, skimming, then drain and cut into small cubes.
instructions.3: Brown the onion in the ghee, then the garlic and peppers.
instructions.4: Add the lungs and stir on high heat until the edges brown, then the tomatoes, paste and spices, stirring until cooked down and dry.
instructions.5: Squeeze over lemon and serve hot with baladi bread.

add-254.title: Egyptian Tripe (Kersha) with Chickpeas
add-254.culturalNotes: Tripe needs careful cleaning and long cooking; a pressure cooker saves a lot of time. The garlic and vinegar dressing is the soul of this Egyptian dish.

add-254-i2.name: For cleaning: coarse salt, vinegar, lemon and flour

add-254-i3.name: For boiling: onion, bay leaves, cardamom and mastic

instructions.1: Scrub the tripe with coarse salt, flour, vinegar and lemon, scrape and rinse several times until white and odour-free.
instructions.2: Blanch 10 minutes and discard the water, then boil in fresh water with the aromatics for 2-3 hours (or an hour in a pressure cooker) until completely tender.
instructions.3: Cut the tripe into small squares, keeping a cup of the broth.
instructions.4: Soften the onion in the ghee, then the garlic, deglaze with the vinegar, then add the tomato juice, spices and broth.
instructions.5: Add the tripe and chickpeas and simmer 20 minutes until thickened.
instructions.6: Serve hot in deep bowls with lemon and bread.

add-255.title: White Bean Salad
add-255.culturalNotes: A salad rich in protein and fibre that makes a light full meal. It improves after an hour in the fridge.

instructions.1: Soak the beans overnight, then boil in fresh water until tender but not mushy; drain and let cool.
instructions.2: Mix the beans with the cucumber, tomato, onion and parsley.
instructions.3: Whisk the lemon, oil, garlic and spices.
instructions.4: Pour the dressing over, toss and leave 15 minutes to absorb the flavours before serving.

add-256.title: Qashtouta (Phyllo Nut Bombs with Ashta)
add-256.culturalNotes: Qashtouta is a modern Egyptian sweet that spread in Ramadan, combining crisp filo with soft ashta and nuts in one bite.

add-256-i4.name: Mixed crushed nuts (pistachio, almond, walnut, hazelnut)

add-256-i6.name: Sugar and cinnamon for the nuts

instructions.1: Mix the nuts with the coconut, sugar and cinnamon.
instructions.2: Cut the filo into large squares and brush 3 layers with ghee, stacking them.
instructions.3: Put a spoon of ashta and a spoon of nuts in the centre, gather the edges up into a parcel (the 'bomb') and press.
instructions.4: Pack the parcels tightly in a greased tray and brush with ghee.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until golden and crisp.
instructions.6: Pour over the cold syrup as soon as they come out and garnish with pistachios.

add-257.title: Harrak Osbao (Lentils with Pasta, Tamarind and Pomegranate)
add-257.culturalNotes: Harrak osbao is a Damascene Lenten dish whose name means 'he burned his finger', because people rush to eat it before it cools. The tang of pomegranate molasses and tamarind sets it apart.

add-257-i2.name: Dough (flour, water, salt) cut into small squares, or small pasta

instructions.1: Boil the lentils in plenty of water until cooked but still holding their shape.
instructions.2: Knead a stiff dough of flour, water and salt, roll thin and cut into small squares; fry half until crisp and keep for garnish.
instructions.3: Add the other half of the dough to the lentils and cook until done and thickened, then add the pomegranate molasses, tamarind, cumin and salt.
instructions.4: Fry half the onions, sliced, in olive oil until brown and crisp; chop the rest and sauté with the garlic and coriander, then add to the lentils.
instructions.5: Spoon into a dish, let it cool slightly, and garnish with the crispy onion, fried dough, toasted bread and coriander; serve warm or cold.

meat-08.title: Grilled Lamb Steaks
meat-08.culturalNotes: This grilled dish showcases the Egyptian love of charred, aromatic meats. Long marination is key to tenderness and flavor absorption.

instructions.1: Season the meat with minced onion, salt, pepper, lemon juice, vinegar, and oil. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, up to 12 hours.
instructions.2: Prepare the grill and place meat pieces with a little oil and seasoned onion to keep them together on the grate. Grill until cooked through.
instructions.3: Transfer meat to a baking dish, cover, and bake in a preheated oven for 1.5 hours until fully cooked.

meat-09.title: Grilled Whole Chicken
meat-09.culturalNotes: This grilled dish showcases the Egyptian love of charred, aromatic meats. Long marination is key to tenderness and flavor absorption.

instructions.1: Split each chicken lengthwise in half and pound well. Marinate in the juice of two grated onions, lemon juice, vinegar, salt and pepper for at least 2 hours.
instructions.2: Brush the pieces with oil or ghee, then grill over charcoal, turning regularly.
instructions.3: Arrange on the serving plate with lemon wedges and fried potatoes.

mp10-8.name: green peppers, tomatoes, and onion for skewering

instructions.1: Cut the chicken into cubes and marinate with the minced onion, salt, pepper, spices, 1 tablespoon of mustard, 2 tablespoons of vinegar, lemon juice, and oil.
instructions.2: Cover and leave in the refrigerator for 4 hours.
instructions.3: Slice the green peppers and cut the onion into quarters, then thread the chicken pieces alternately with the vegetables onto skewers.
instructions.4: Grill the chicken over charcoal, and just before finishing, thread the tomatoes onto skewers to cook quickly.

meat-11.title: Beef Fillet or Chicken Breast in Broth

mp11-8.name: Vinegar, lemon juice, and ghee
mp11-8.standardAmount: 1 tbsp vinegar - juice of 1 lemon - 2 tbsp ghee

instructions.1: Season the meat or chicken with black pepper.
instructions.2: Prepare a pan with 2 tbsp of oil and one whole small onion, then sear the meat or chicken.
instructions.3: Sauté the minced garlic with finely chopped parsley or chopped green pepper, a little water, and salt; leave it on very low heat, adding water whenever necessary until it is cooked and the liquid is fully absorbed.
instructions.4: Additional method: Add 1 tbsp vinegar, the juice of one lemon, 2 tbsp ghee or oil, salt, and pepper to the meat or chicken, and leave it on very low heat while stirring continuously.
instructions.5: Gradually add water whenever needed until cooked, then remove the cooked meat.
instructions.6: Fry the two cubed potatoes, then place them in the sauce until they absorb the flavor.

meat-12.title: Meat with Green Peppers
meat-12.culturalNotes: This is a traditional Egyptian dish prepared with fresh ingredients and aromatic spices.

instructions.1: Slice the meat along with the onion and green peppers.
instructions.2: Brown the meat in oil or ghee, then set it aside.
instructions.3: Add the onion and sauté, then add the green peppers, return the meat to the pot, and season with salt and pepper, adding a little water as needed, covered, until cooked through.

meat-13.title: Lamb with Cumin (Kammuniya)
meat-13.culturalNotes: This spiced meat dish is a cornerstone of Egyptian home cooking, with cumin providing its distinctive warm, earthy note.

instructions.1: Cut the meat into small pieces and brown it in oil or ghee.
instructions.2: Add the crushed garlic in proportion to the meat, then add the cumin, and stir until the garlic turns golden.
instructions.3: Add a cup and a half of water with the tablespoon of vinegar and the whole onion, and simmer over low heat until cooked through.

meat-14.title: Meat with Tear Sauce
meat-14.culturalNotes: This is a traditional Egyptian dish prepared with fresh ingredients and aromatic spices.

instructions.1: Cut the meat into medium pieces and brown it in oil or ghee, then add the crushed garlic and stir until golden, then season with salt and pepper.
instructions.2: Blend the tomatoes and add them to the meat until the sauce thickens and cooks down.
instructions.3: Add the vinegar and stir well, then add about 2 cups of water, and simmer over low heat until fully cooked.

meat-15.title: Pan-Seared Beef
meat-15.culturalNotes: This is a traditional Egyptian dish prepared with fresh ingredients and aromatic spices.

instructions.1: Marinate the meat in onion juice, lemon juice or vinegar, salt and pepper.
instructions.2: Place the marinated meat in a pot with oil or ghee over low heat, covered, until it absorbs its own liquid; add a little more oil or ghee and stir until browned, then add water until fully cooked.

instructions.1: Slice the beef lengthwise into strips and season with salt, pepper, and spices.
instructions.2: Heat the oil or ghee in a pot, add the beef slices until browned, then remove them from the pot.
instructions.3: In the same pot, add the sliced onion and sauté, then add the beef slices along with the tablespoon of tomato paste; cover and leave over low heat.
instructions.4: Add water whenever the beef needs it until it is nearly cooked through.
instructions.5: Add the half cup of milk to the beef over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.

instructions.1: Season the chicken with black pepper.
instructions.2: Heat the oil or ghee in a pan and sear all the chicken at once over high heat; flip to brown the other side, then remove from the pan.
instructions.3: In the same pan, add the finely chopped onions and the minced garlic and sauté, then add some water and salt and bring to a boil.
instructions.4: Finely chop the green pepper and mix it with the half cup of cream and the tablespoon of mustard, stirring well (the cream can be replaced with 1 tbsp of dissolved clotted cream mixed with a little milk).
instructions.5: Add the seared chicken to this mixture, return it to the pan, cover, and simmer over low heat until cooked through.

instructions.1: Season the chicken in the flour mixed with cumin, coriander, and salt.
instructions.2: Fry in oil until golden brown, then remove from the pan.
instructions.3: In the same pan, sauté the finely chopped onion, then add the minced garlic, salt, pepper, and thyme while stirring.
instructions.4: Add the tomato juice or tomato paste and cook until thickened, then place the chicken on top of the sauce, cover the pan, and add a little water if needed until cooked through.
instructions.5: Just before finishing, sprinkle with a little chopped parsley.

instructions.1: Marinate the chicken with only the juice of half the onion along with salt and pepper, then leave covered in the refrigerator for at least two hours.
instructions.2: Coat the chicken in flour, ensuring both sides are well-covered, then fry in oil until golden brown and remove from the pan.
instructions.3: Mix the minced garlic and minced cardamom with salt, pepper, and cinnamon, then sauté them in the same oil.
instructions.4: Finely dice the remaining half of the onion and sauté it with the aromatics.
instructions.5: Add the milk and water and bring to a boil, then place the fried chicken into the liquid and simmer until cooked, ensuring a little white sauce remains.

meat-20.title: Curry Chicken
meat-20.culturalNotes: Curry represents global influences in modern Egyptian cuisine, adding warm complexity to traditional dishes.

instructions.1: Cut the chicken into small pieces and sauté in very hot oil, covered while browning, until golden, then lift out of the oil.
instructions.2: Mix the flour with the curry powder, then gradually add 2 cups of water until it reaches a medium consistency.
instructions.3: Return the chicken to this mixture and simmer covered over low heat until cooked through.

instructions.1: Slice the beef into small strips and season with salt, pepper, and vinegar or lemon juice.
instructions.2: Sauté the seasoned beef strips in oil over low heat, covering the pan, and leave until half-cooked.
instructions.3: Dice the onions into small squares along with the tomato, green pepper, minced garlic, and chopped or minced parsley.
instructions.4: Add this mixture to the meat and cook until fully tender.
instructions.5: Dissolve 2 tbsp of tahini in 1 tbsp of vinegar, then gradually dilute with water until the desired consistency is reached, seasoning with salt and pepper.
instructions.6: Pour the tahini sauce over the meat, give it one quick stir, and remove from the stove.

meat-22.title: Shawarma with Spice Blend
meat-22.culturalNotes: This grilled dish showcases the Egyptian love of charred, aromatic meats. Long marination is key to tenderness and flavor absorption.

instructions.1: Cut the meat into thin, finger-like strips, then place it in a pot with oil over low heat, covered, without any seasoning, until it fully absorbs its own liquid.
instructions.2: Add enough water to cover it, and once the meat has absorbed about three-quarters of the water, add the spice packet and stir well.
instructions.3: Cut the tomato and green pepper into small pieces and add them to the meat with just one stir.

meat-23.title: Breaded Meat or Chicken Cutlets (Babtik)
meat-23.culturalNotes: Breaded cutlets (babtik) blend Egyptian home cooking traditions with European-style preparation techniques.

instructions.1: Pound the boneless meat or chicken pieces well, then season with salt, pepper, coriander, crushed garlic and thyme, along with onion juice and lemon juice (or any of the frying marinades).
instructions.2: Refrigerate for at least an hour.
instructions.3: Lift out of the marinade and coat in flour, then dip in egg beaten with salt and pepper, then coat in breadcrumbs, and fry in oil.
instructions.4: Vinegar, crushed cardamom, and a small amount of milk can be added to the marinade above.

meat-24.title: Soy-Marinated Chicken Breasts
meat-24.culturalNotes: This is a traditional Egyptian dish prepared with fresh ingredients and aromatic spices.

instructions.1: Cut the chicken into thin slices and marinate with onion, salt, pepper and mixed spice, then add soy sauce in proportion to the chicken, along with lemon juice or vinegar.
instructions.2: Refrigerate for 3 hours.
instructions.3: Coat the marinated chicken in flour or cornstarch, then fry it in oil.

meat-25.title: Chicken Rissoles
meat-25.culturalNotes: This is a traditional Egyptian dish prepared with fresh ingredients and aromatic spices.

instructions.1: Mince the chicken and add breadcrumbs, then season with salt, pepper and lemon juice (or any of the frying marinades).
instructions.2: Knead in the egg and mix well until it forms a firm dough.
instructions.3: Shape into balls or fingers, as preferred.
instructions.4: Dip in egg, then breadcrumbs, and fry in oil.

mp26-7.name: eggs
mp26-7.standardAmount: 1 egg for the mixture + 1 for coating

instructions.1: Sauté the small minced onion in oil or ghee, then add the flour and cook until just golden, then remove from heat.
instructions.2: Off the heat, add the cup of milk along with the salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Return to medium heat and stir until the mixture thickens.
instructions.4: Season the cooked minced chicken with salt, pepper, and nutmeg, then mix it with the white sauce (bechamel).
instructions.5: Remove the pan from the heat, add one egg, and stir well.
instructions.6: Let the mixture cool completely, divide it into 6 pieces, and shape them into cutlet shapes.
instructions.7: Dip the pieces in a little flour, then coat with egg and breadcrumbs, and fry in oil.

mp27-3.name: salt, pepper, coriander, thyme, and cardamom

instructions.1: Cut the chicken into small pieces and season it in a mixture of flour, eggs, and milk; mix well, then add the blended green pepper and the spices.
instructions.2: Place in the refrigerator for 2 hours.
instructions.3: Coat in breadcrumbs and fry all pieces in plenty of oil once, then remove from heat, and fry a second time until golden yellow.
instructions.4: Serve with garlic sauce (Toum) (see salads section).
instructions.5: After boiling the chicken and cutting it into quarters, pound them lightly, then coat in flour mixed with a little baking powder, spices, mustard, and a little milk or water, and fry in oil.

meat-28.title: Egyptian Kentucky-Style Fried Chicken
meat-28.culturalNotes: This is a traditional Egyptian dish prepared with fresh ingredients and aromatic spices.

instructions.1: Marinate the chicken pieces in grated onion mashed with salt, pepper and mixed spice.
instructions.2: Coat the chicken pieces in flour mixed with cornstarch, then refrigerate for 3 hours.
instructions.3: Dip in egg, then breadcrumbs, refrigerate again until firm, then fry in oil.

instructions.1: After boiling the chicken, cut it into quarters and squeeze over it an onion rubbed with salt, pepper, spices, and the lemon juice.
instructions.2: Place in the refrigerator for at least one hour until well marinated.
instructions.3: Whisk 2 eggs with the milk, salt, pepper, and spices, then gradually add the flour using a whisk.
instructions.4: Place the chicken in the mixture and let it sit until it absorbs some of the liquid.
instructions.5: Fry in oil on both sides.
instructions.6: Season raw chicken with lemon juice and refrigerate for a full day, then make a mixture of 2 tbsp flour, a little milk, and garlic powder; dip the chicken pieces in it and fry thoroughly in oil.

instructions.1: Sauté the onion in oil, then add the pepper and garlic until they turn golden.
instructions.2: Mix the ground beef with the eggs and flour, kneading well, and season with spices.
instructions.3: Add the sautéed onion mixture to the ground beef and knead thoroughly.
instructions.4: Shape the mixture into balls, flatten them into circles, and dredge in flour.
instructions.5: Fry in very hot oil for only a few seconds, then flip to the other side just until they firm up.
instructions.6: After light frying, cover the patties with layers of foil and stack them in the freezer until frozen; when ready to use, lightly grease a tray with oil, arrange the patties, and place in the oven until heated through.
instructions.7: Alternatively, grease a tray with oil, line the bottom with sliced peppers, arrange the patties on top, and bake in the oven until cooked through.

meat-31.title: Chicken Hamburger
meat-31.culturalNotes: Egyptian hamburgers are boldly seasoned with onions and spices, pan-fried to create juicy patties with caramelized edges.

instructions.1: Shred the boiled chicken and mix with the onion, crushed garlic, egg and oil, season with the spices (or any frying marinade), and shape into patties.
instructions.2: After mixing well, cover and refrigerate for 2 hours.
instructions.3: Lightly oil a non-stick pan and cook the patties over medium heat, turning, until done.

meat-32.title: Spiced Chicken Kofta
meat-32.culturalNotes: This spiced meat dish is a cornerstone of Egyptian home cooking, with cumin providing its distinctive warm, earthy note.

instructions.1: Knead the minced leftover chicken with the grated onion, salt, pepper and lemon juice, and refrigerate for an hour.
instructions.2: Shape into fingers or patties.
instructions.3: Coat in flour, then dip in beaten egg, then coat in breadcrumbs.
instructions.4: Deep-fry in oil or ghee.

mp33-6.name: minced garlic and parsley
mp33-6.standardAmount: 2 cloves garlic and a little parsley

instructions.1: Soak the Baladi bread in a little water until soft, then squeeze it thoroughly to remove all excess water.
instructions.2: Mix the bread well with the ground beef, then season with salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Grate the onion and squeeze it thoroughly to remove the liquid, using only the grated pulp; mix it well into the meat, then add the eggs (depending on the consistency of the mixture) along with the minced garlic and parsley, and knead well.
instructions.4: Form into small balls, then flatten them into discs.
instructions.5: Lightly coat the discs in breadcrumbs first, then use a brush to coat both sides with egg.
instructions.6: Fry in oil until golden brown.

mp34-6.name: salt, pepper, spices, and dried mint
mp34-6.standardAmount: 1 tsp mint, remaining spices to taste

instructions.1: After boiling the rice, drain it well, let it cool, and then process it in a food processor.
instructions.2: Season the ground beef with the onion, garlic, salt, pepper, and spices.
instructions.3: Mix the seasoned meat with the boiled rice and knead well with the egg.
instructions.4: Shape the mixture into fingers or rounds.
instructions.5: Steam until the shapes firm up, then let them cool.
instructions.6: Coat with egg and breadcrumbs, then fry in oil.
instructions.7: You can skip the steaming step by dredging the kofta fingers or rounds in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, and letting them rest in the refrigerator for one hour until firm before frying in oil.

mp35-7.name: vegetable sauce
mp35-7.standardAmount: the amount produced by the following recipe

instructions.1: Pulse the ground beef, onion, parsley, and dill in a food processor, then add the crushed rice and spices; blend until the mixture becomes thick.
instructions.2: Shape the mixture into small balls and fry them in oil.
instructions.3: Place the kofta in the sauce and let it simmer on low heat for 15 minutes.

meat-36.title: Making Vegetable Sauce
meat-36.servings: enough for a Kofta Rice casserole

instructions.1: Heat the oil and sauté the garlic only until golden, then add the tomato puree; season with salt, pepper, and vinegar, then remove from heat.
instructions.2: Prepare a pot with about 3 cups of boiling water, salt, and pepper, then add the finely diced carrots and cook for 15 minutes.
instructions.3: Add the diced potatoes to the carrots in the boiling water, then pour in the tomato sauce; cook over medium heat for 15 minutes until the sauce thickens.

mp37-2.name: medium onion, minced or onion juice

mp37-8.name: dam'a (soft tomato sauce)
mp37-8.standardAmount: the amount produced by the following recipe

instructions.1: Mix the ground meat with the onion (or onion juice), garlic, parsley, and spices.
instructions.2: Refrigerate for 1 hour.
instructions.3: Wash the rice and drain it thoroughly until completely dry, then process it in a food processor until fine.
instructions.4: Mix the ground rice thoroughly with the ground meat.
instructions.5: Shape into fingers or rounds as desired.
instructions.6: Steam until the kofta sets.
instructions.7: Remove and let cool, then fry in oil.
instructions.8: Place the fried kofta fingers into the dam'a, cover the pot, and cook over low heat until the kofta is cooked through and has absorbed some of the sauce.

instructions.1: Lightly sauté the garlic in ghee or oil, then add the tomato puree and cook until thickened.
instructions.2: Add the tablespoon of vinegar and stir well, then add the water and season with salt and pepper; bring to a boil.

mp39-6.name: prepared tomato sauce (starch recipe)
mp39-6.standardAmount: the amount produced from the sauce recipe

instructions.1: Season the ground meat with dill, garlic, breadcrumbs, and spices, then knead well.
instructions.2: Shape into fingers or rounds as desired.
instructions.3: Brown in oil or ghee.
instructions.4: Prepare a sauce similar to pasta sauce (starch section).
instructions.5: Once the sauce comes to a boil, add the kofta and simmer on low heat until cooked through.

mp40-6.name: Asag (minced meat filling with pine nuts)
mp40-6.standardAmount: the amount produced from the Asag recipe

instructions.1: Finely mince the meat with a little salt, then mince the onions and add them to the minced meat and process twice more.
instructions.2: Wash the bulgur several times and drain it thoroughly.
instructions.3: Add the bulgur to the minced meat, mix well, and season with spices, then process this mixture twice more.
instructions.4: Shape the mixture into egg-sized pieces, press a hole in the center with your finger, fill with a portion of the Asag, and seal it so that it remains hollow.
instructions.5: Fry in oil or ghee.
instructions.6: Additional method: After preparing and filling the kibbeh as described above, grease a tray and place half of the kibbeh mixture in it, then add a layer of Asag and pine nuts, then top with the remaining kibbeh mixture. Drizzle the surface with ghee or butter and cut into samosa-like shapes, then bake in a medium oven until cooked through and lightly browned on top.

instructions.1: Heat the ghee or oil and sauté the onion, then add the ground beef and spices, and cook over low heat until done, adding water as needed.

meat-42.title: Yogurt Marinade
meat-42.servings: enough for 1 kg meat or chicken

instructions.1: Blend the tomato, carrot, garlic, and celery in a blender, then add the yogurt, salt, and pepper.
instructions.2: Fry a sliced onion in oil, then add it to the mixture.
instructions.3: Marinate meat or chicken in this mixture.

meat-43.title: Tomato Sauce Marinade
meat-43.servings: enough for 1 kg of meat or chicken

mp43-5.name: salt, pepper, mixed spices, thyme, cinnamon, cloves, and cardamom

mp43-8.name: tomatoes or tomato paste and water

instructions.1: Pulse the onions, garlic, bell pepper, and all spices in a food processor.
instructions.2: Add the blended tomatoes or tomato paste and the oil, then mix well with the lemon juice.
instructions.3: Marinate the meat or chicken in this mixture.
instructions.4: Grease a baking tray with oil, place the marinated meat inside with a little water, cover, and bake in the oven.

meat-44.title: Meat or Chicken in Baking Dish (Rostopatllo)

mp44-8.name: Salt, pepper, mixed spices, thyme, cinnamon, cloves, and cardamom

instructions.1: Brown the meat or chicken in a pan with oil or ghee until golden, then transfer to a baking tray.
instructions.2: Season one large sliced onion with salt, pepper, mixed spices, cinnamon, thyme, and cloves, then add it to the meat in the tray, or use any oven-roasting seasoning.
instructions.3: Slice the green pepper and combine it with the minced garlic and tomato juice (or 2 tbsp of tomato paste diluted with water), then add to the meat or chicken.
instructions.4: Add an appropriate amount of water mixed with lemon juice or vinegar and crushed cardamom, bring to a boil, then drizzle oil on top.
instructions.5: Cover the tray with foil and place in the oven until cooked; near the end of cooking, remove the cover and leave the tray until all the liquid is fully absorbed.

meat-45.title: Meat or Chicken Baked with Vegetables

instructions.1: Steam the carrots, zucchini, and potatoes that have been cut into very small cubes.
instructions.2: Make a mixture of onion rings, green pepper, cheddar cheese slices, olives, salt, and pepper.
instructions.3: Add this mixture to the steamed vegetables and knead well.
instructions.4: Grease a baking tray with oil, spread a layer of the vegetable mixture, then add a layer of the meat or chicken.
instructions.5: Brush the top with beaten egg and sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
instructions.6: Cover and place in the oven.

meat-46.title: Baked Pan-Seared Chicken
meat-46.culturalNotes: Baked casserole dishes (sanyia) are weeknight staples in Egyptian homes, combining meat, vegetables, and sauce in one dish.

instructions.1: Mix the flour well with the cumin, coriander, salt and pepper.
instructions.2: Quarter the chicken and coat it in the mixture.
instructions.3: Brown in oil until golden, then drain on paper towels.
instructions.4: Oil a tray, arrange the chicken in it, cover, and bake.

mp47-5.name: salt, pepper, mixed spices, and cinnamon

instructions.1: Sear the leg in a tray with oil or ghee along with sliced onions that have been rubbed with salt, pepper, mixed spices, and cinnamon.
instructions.2: Pierce whole garlic cloves into the leg, or simply place them around it without piercing.
instructions.3: Add the onion juice and vinegar to the leg.
instructions.4: Wrap the tray tightly in foil and pour a little water around the meat.
instructions.5: Place in the oven, adding more water as needed until fully cooked.

instructions.1: Blend the onion, salt, pepper, garlic, tomatoes, and spices in a blender, then add the yogurt, or use any of your preferred oven roasting marinades.
instructions.2: Make a deep opening next to the bone and pour half of the mixture into it.
instructions.3: Flip the leg to the other side, apply the rest of the marinade, and then add the oil.
instructions.4: Wrap in foil, place in a baking dish, and put in the oven until cooked through.
instructions.5: Once the leg is cooked, pour the remaining sauce into a small pot. Mix the cornstarch or flour with a little water (proportional to the amount of sauce) and pour it into the sauce over low heat, stirring until it thickens.
instructions.6: Open the foil and pour the thickened sauce over the leg.
instructions.7: Serve with sautéed vegetables on the side.

meat-49.title: Meat or Chicken in Yogurt Sauce

mp49-8.name: Salt, pepper, mixed spices, and thyme

instructions.1: Blend the tomato, onion, pepper, garlic, lemon juice or vinegar, mustard, spices, and yogurt in a blender, or use any oven-roasting marinade.
instructions.2: Place the meat or chicken in a greased baking dish, pour the mixture over it, cover, and refrigerate for 4 hours.
instructions.3: Place the dish in the oven at medium heat, adding a little water if necessary, until cooked through.
instructions.4: Remove the cover and leave it in the oven until the liquid is completely absorbed.

meat-50.title: Rolled Roasted Meat
meat-50.culturalNotes: This is a traditional Egyptian dish prepared with fresh ingredients and aromatic spices.

instructions.1: Slice the onion into rings and mash it with salt, pepper and mixed spice.
instructions.2: Cut the meat into small, even pieces and drizzle with the oil.
instructions.3: Mix the meat with the mashed onion and oil, wrap in foil, and seal well.
instructions.4: Bake for about 2 hours, until fully cooked.

mp51-1.name: minced meat or leftover boiled chicken

mp51-6.name: salt, pepper, thyme, mixed spices, and turmeric

instructions.1: Prepare a food processor to mince the meat or leftover chicken with the grated carrot, green pepper, and spices.
instructions.2: Add one beaten egg and half a cup of milk to the mixture and mix well.
instructions.3: Prepare a mold, grease it with oil, and press the mixture into it.
instructions.4: Place in the oven at medium heat, and once cooked, cut into slices.

mp52-8.name: salt, pepper, mixed spices, thyme, cinnamon, and cloves

instructions.1: Grease a baking dish with oil, cut the boiled chicken into quarters, and place it in the dish.
instructions.2: Slice the onion and sauté in oil in a pan until golden.
instructions.3: Slice the pepper and add it to the onions along with the minced garlic; sauté well, then add the vinegar and spices.
instructions.4: Add one cup of broth or water to the mixture; once boiling, pour it over the chicken and place in a medium oven until the liquid is absorbed and the top is browned.

instructions.1: Prepare a baking dish or Pyrex and spread a layer of cornflakes at the bottom to serve as a base.
instructions.2: Cut the chicken into small pieces, and slice the olives and green pepper.
instructions.3: Place the chicken, olives, and pepper on top of the cornflakes.
instructions.4: Make a thick béchamel sauce by heating the oil and adding the flour; once it turns golden, add the cup of milk along with salt and pepper while off the heat and stir, then return to medium heat until the consistency thickens.
instructions.5: Pour the béchamel over the chicken and sprinkle shredded Rumi cheese on top.
instructions.6: Sprinkle a small amount of cornflakes over the shredded cheese, cover, and place in the oven.

meat-54.title: Mustard-Glazed Chicken
meat-54.culturalNotes: This is a traditional Egyptian dish prepared with fresh ingredients and aromatic spices.

instructions.1: Slice the chicken breasts thinly and brown in hot oil until golden, then remove and arrange in a tray.
instructions.2: In the same pot, add more oil or ghee, whisk in the mustard quickly over low heat, then whisk in the clotted cream dissolved in milk, and add water as needed.
instructions.3: Once it boils, pour the sauce over the chicken in the tray, cover, and bake until fully cooked.

instructions.1: Slice the chicken breasts and sauté them in oil until golden, then remove from heat.
instructions.2: Season the grated onion with salt, pepper, spices, and vinegar, then spread it over the chicken in a baking dish.
instructions.3: Sprinkle any type of shredded cheese over the chicken and mix well with the meat.
instructions.4: Pour the cup of cream over the top and bake in the oven until cooked through and the top is golden brown.

mp56-3.name: salt, pepper, mixed spices, and thyme

instructions.1: Rub the sliced onions with salt, pepper, mixed spices, and thyme.
instructions.2: Add the tablespoon of ghee and the breadcrumbs, mixing well, then knead with milk until the mixture becomes soft.
instructions.3: Stuff the duck with this mixture and place it in a baking tray greased with oil or ghee; drizzle some ghee or oil over the top and cover with foil.
instructions.4: Place in a medium-heat oven until cooked through, then remove the foil to allow the skin to brown.

instructions.1: Finely mince the onion with the garlic and bay leaves, then season with the spices and add plenty of lemon juice.
instructions.2: Season the turkey thoroughly inside and out, then refrigerate for one full day.
instructions.3: Prepare a baking tray greased with oil, place the marinated turkey inside, and cover it with foil.
instructions.4: Place in the oven for approximately 2 hours, making sure to flip it onto the other side halfway through.
instructions.5: Once cooked, slice the turkey and arrange the pieces on a serving platter.

instructions.1: Mix the meat with the minced onion, lemon juice, and spices, then leave it in the refrigerator for 12 hours.
instructions.2: Knead the mixture with the egg and breadcrumbs until the desired consistency is reached.
instructions.3: Shape the kofta into medium-sized fingers, piercing them with a skewer to create a hole.
instructions.4: Grease the tray with ghee and arrange the kofta fingers inside, then add 2 tablespoons of ghee on top; cover and bake in a medium-heat oven.
instructions.5: Once cooked, char a piece of charcoal thoroughly on the stove, place it in the middle of the tray on a little ghee, cover immediately, and shake the tray until the charcoal aroma spreads throughout.

instructions.1: Rub the chopped onion with the vinegar, garlic, yogurt, and mustard.
instructions.2: Cut the boiled chicken into small pieces and mix thoroughly with the mixture.
instructions.3: Sauté in a pan without oil over low heat until the onion liquid is absorbed, then increase the heat.
instructions.4: Prepare a tray greased with oil and place the chicken in it; then slice the pepper and tomato and place them on top of the chicken with the lemon juice, vinegar, and parsley to prevent the chicken from drying out.
instructions.5: To brown the top, you can place the tray under the broiler for a very short time.

instructions.1: Season the ground chicken well with salt, pepper, chopped bell pepper, cheese, and tahini.
instructions.2: Prepare a sheet of phyllo pastry brushed with butter, place a portion of the chicken mixture inside, and roll it into triangles, brushing the outside with butter.
instructions.3: Place in a lightly greased baking dish and repeat with the remaining phyllo sheets.
instructions.4: Bake in a medium-heat oven until the top is golden brown.

instructions.1: Melt the ghee or oil, add the flour, and stir well until it turns slightly golden, then remove the pan from the heat.
instructions.2: Gradually add the milk or broth while off the heat, stirring constantly until smooth, then return the pan to the stove over medium heat until it reaches the desired thickness, ensuring the sauce remains slightly fluid.
instructions.3: Season with salt and pepper.
instructions.4: Variation with parsley or lemon: Optionally, add 1 tsp of chopped parsley or 1 tsp of lemon juice to the sauce while it is still hot.
instructions.5: Variation with mustard and vinegar (Method 1): Alternatively, mix 1 tsp of mustard well with 1 tbsp of vinegar, add it to the sauce, and bring it back to a boil on the stove.
instructions.6: Variation with mustard and vinegar (Method 2): Or, add 1 tsp of mustard directly to the sauce and stir well, then let it cool; subsequently, gradually whisk in 1 tbsp of oil alternating with 1 tbsp of vinegar, stirring constantly until emulsified.

instructions.1: Prepare the fish and lightly fry it in oil (half-fry only), then remove it from the oil and set aside.
instructions.2: Sauté the sliced onions in the same oil until they turn golden, then add the minced garlic and dried coriander and stir.
instructions.3: Add the blended tomatoes and leave over low heat, seasoning with salt as needed, and adding a little water if necessary until the tomatoes cook down and thicken into a sauce.
instructions.4: Place the lightly fried fish into the sauce, cover the pot, and leave over low heat until cooked through.
instructions.5: Oven method (alternative): You can replace the pot with a baking dish, place the same ingredients inside, cover, and bake in the oven until cooked instead of cooking on the stovetop.
instructions.6: Serving: Serve with tahini salad or a white seafood sauce.

instructions.1: Clean and butterfly the fish: Clean the fish and butterfly it by making a wide longitudinal cut along the belly (without separating the two halves), then season both the inside and outside with the chopped onion, minced garlic, spices, and lemon juice.
instructions.2: Prepare the filling: Slice the tomatoes and green peppers into thin rings.
instructions.3: Stuff and marinate: Place the tomato and green pepper rings inside the opened belly of the fish and let the stuffed fish sit for a while to absorb the marinade.
instructions.4: Baking: Grease a baking tray and arrange the fish in it, drizzle a little oil and lemon juice over the top, then place in the oven until fully cooked and golden brown.
instructions.5: Serving: Serve with tahini salad or a white seafood sauce.

instructions.1: Sauté the onion in oil, then add the garlic and chopped tomatoes; add about 1 cup of water with the sugar and let it boil for approximately 5 minutes over medium heat.
instructions.2: Grease a baking dish with oil and pour in the sautéed onion along with its liquid.
instructions.3: Cut the potatoes into medium cubes and add them to the sauce in the baking dish along with 2 tablespoons of tomato paste.
instructions.4: Prepare a light white sauce: In the same first pot, melt the butter and stir in the flour well, then add the spices, celery, and parsley with enough water to reach a medium consistency (it is preferable to keep it thin if the potatoes are being cooked with the fish).
instructions.5: Place the fish pieces into this white sauce, then pour the mixture over the sauce and potatoes in the baking dish.
instructions.6: Cover the dish and place it in the oven until cooked through, reserving a little sauce to pour over the fish when serving.
instructions.7: Serving: Serve with tahini salad or a white seafood sauce.

instructions.1: Cleaning: Clean the squid with hot water and wash very thoroughly, then toss with vinegar and place in a strainer for one minute.
instructions.2: If the squid is large, bring water to a boil, drop the squid in for just one single boil, then drain.
instructions.3: Cut the squid into rings or long strips, trimming off the ends.
instructions.4: Seasoning: Place in a deep bowl and season with vinegar, salt, pepper, cumin, and the juice of the two lemons; let marinate for at least one hour.
instructions.5: Place in a strainer to dry completely from excess water and marinade, then dredge the rings in flour.
instructions.6: Fry the rings in plenty of oil until golden.
instructions.7: Serving: Serve with tahini salad or white seafood sauce.

sf10-4.name: cumin, black pepper, mastic, and cardamom

instructions.1: Wash the shrimp several times to ensure all sand is completely removed.
instructions.2: Slice the onions into rings and layer them in the pot, alternating with the shrimp, celery, spices, a little salt, and lemon juice.
instructions.3: You may add a little water if the shrimp are large in size.
instructions.4: Cover the pot and place it over low heat, stirring constantly until cooked through.
instructions.5: Remove the pot from the heat and shake it well so the shrimp do not stick together.
instructions.6: Serve as desired, either in the shell or peeled, with tahini salad or a white seafood sauce.

instructions.1: Wash the shrimp several times to ensure all sand is completely removed.
instructions.2: Slice the onions into rings and layer them in a pot, alternating with the shrimp, celery, mastic, cardamom, and a little salt.
instructions.3: You may add a little water if the shrimp are large.
instructions.4: Cover the pot and cook over low heat, stirring constantly until cooked through.
instructions.5: Remove the pot from the heat and shake well so the shrimp do not stick together.
instructions.6: Drain and peel the shrimp, then season with salt, pepper, cumin, and lemon juice.
instructions.7: Arrange in a serving dish and top with the mayonnaise sauce (see the Salads section).

instructions.1: Initial preparation: Wash the shrimp several times to completely remove any sand. Slice the onions into rings and layer them alternately with the shrimp, celery, mastic, cardamom, and a pinch of salt in a pot (you may add a little water if the pot is large).
instructions.2: Cover the pot and cook over low heat, stirring constantly until cooked through. Remove from heat and shake well to prevent sticking, then pat the shrimp dry and peel them.
instructions.3: Curry sauce: Sauté the sliced onions in oil until golden, then add the curry powder and stir briefly. Add the water and stir until boiling, then season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
instructions.4: Add the peeled shrimp to the curry sauce just until heated through.
instructions.5: Serving: Ladle into a serving dish alongside white rice, and garnish with lemon and parsley.

instructions.1: Toast the vermicelli or orzo in the ghee.
instructions.2: Pour in the salted broth with pepper and bring to a boil, then lower the heat until cooked (orzo takes longer to cook and may require extra broth).
instructions.3: For extra flavor, you can add mastic to the broth.

instructions.1: Sauté the onion in butter or ghee, then add the flour and stir. Gradually add the broth or water along with the bouillon cube, and let it simmer on low heat until it reaches a boil.
instructions.2: Once cooled, blend the mixture in a blender. Return it to the pot and add the cream, cooked chicken pieces, and milk (adjusting the amount of milk to reach your desired thickness), then season with salt and pepper.
instructions.3: The chicken pieces can be replaced with shredded cheese.
instructions.4: Ensure the soup is served very hot.

instructions.1: Sauté the sliced onion in butter until golden.
instructions.2: Add the chopped tomato along with the tomato paste and flour, and mix well with the onions.
instructions.3: Pour the broth over the mixture and cook on low heat until done.
instructions.4: Once the mixture has cooled, blend it in a blender.
instructions.5: Whisk a little milk with the egg yolk and salt and pepper, pour it over the blended soup, then return to the pot over low heat for 5 minutes.

instructions.1: Whisk the egg with the salt, pepper, lemon juice, and vinegar thoroughly using a wire whisk.
instructions.2: Carefully add the oil drop by drop until the consistency thickens somewhat.
instructions.3: Place the mayonnaise in a bowl, add the mustard, and mix well.
instructions.4: Transfer to a very dry jar and refrigerate.

salad-04.title: Chicken Salad with Mayonnaise and Toast

instructions.1: After boiling the chicken, cut it into small strips.
instructions.2: Mix the yogurt with the mayonnaise and olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and mix well.
instructions.3: Toast the cubed toast slices in the oven until they turn golden brown.
instructions.4: Pour the mayonnaise mixture over the sliced chicken and serve in a serving dish with the toasted croutons.

instructions.1: Add the garlic to the yogurt along with the salt, pepper, and mint, and whisk well.
instructions.2: Place the salad in a bowl and add small pieces of chopped cucumber, or substitute with a little chopped parsley.

salad-06.title: Garlic and Vinegar Dressing (for Fried Eggplant or Grilled Fish)

instructions.1: Mince the garlic with the cumin and salt, then add the vinegar and mix well.
instructions.2: Serve this salad with fried eggplant and grilled fish.

instructions.1: Chop the green pepper and place it in a blender with the garlic, salt, cumin, vinegar, and lemon juice; then add the boiled chickpeas with the yogurt, followed by the tahini and dried mint.
instructions.2: Blend all ingredients thoroughly, then transfer to a serving dish.
instructions.3: Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with chopped parsley.

instructions.1: Dice the tomatoes and cucumbers, then add the chopped parsley, dried mint, and finely sliced lettuce leaves along with the lemon juice; season the mixture with salt, pepper, and vinegar.
instructions.2: Toast the Shami bread after cutting it into small pieces.
instructions.3: Place the salad in a serving dish, add the black olives, and then top with the toasted bread.

instructions.1: Whisk the mustard with the eggs, either by beating the yolks and whites separately or by beating the whole eggs together.
instructions.2: Add the minced garlic and oil and whisk them well, then add to the egg and mustard mixture and season with salt, whisking thoroughly until the mixture is smooth and reaches a caramel-like consistency.

instructions.1: Mix the boiled vegetables together, then season with half of the mayonnaise sauce.
instructions.2: Pour into a serving dish, cover the surface with the remaining sauce, and garnish with cucumber.

instructions.1: Wash the potatoes thoroughly with their skins on.
instructions.2: Boil the potatoes in salted boiling water until tender, being careful not to let them become mushy.
instructions.3: Peel the potatoes and cut them into medium-sized cubes.
instructions.4: In a deep bowl, prepare the dressing by mixing the oil with salt and cumin, then add the onion juice, minced garlic, and lemon juice or vinegar, and mix well.
instructions.5: Chop the tomatoes and green peppers into medium pieces, finely chop the parsley, then add them to the dressing and mix well.
instructions.6: Add the potato cubes to the mixture and toss well.
instructions.7: Place in the refrigerator until serving time.
instructions.8: General tips for preserving vegetables: Blanch chopped vegetables for freezing by boiling them for one minute in salted water with a little baking soda, then immediately drain in ice water, dry, and pack in airtight bags in the freezer for no more than 3 months (pour directly into hot soup while frozen). To preserve molokhia, after chopping, submerge it in a ladle of broth before freezing. Artichokes are preserved in the refrigerator in boiled water with olive oil and plenty of lemon juice. Potato slices should be boiled for 3-4 minutes, then cooled in water and vinegar before drying and freezing; fry them while still frozen.

instructions.1: Heat about 2 tbsp of oil in a pot over medium heat, add the large grated onion and the meat, and sauté until the meat browns.
instructions.2: Add the vinegar, minced garlic, and either the pureed tomatoes or tomato paste; cook until the tomatoes are softened if using fresh, then season with salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Add water, and once it reaches a boil, add the vegetables and spices, then simmer on low heat until everything is tender.

instructions.1: Boil the chicken in boiling water with the onion, cardamom, mastic, salt, and pepper.
instructions.2: Remove the chicken and place it in a strainer, then season with salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Blend the large onion, approximately ¼ kg of tomatoes, one small green bell pepper, the garlic cloves, and the tablespoon of vinegar in a blender.
instructions.4: Prepare a cooking pot and add 2 tbsp of oil (or as desired); once the oil is hot, pour in the blended mixture, season with salt and pepper, and let it come to a boil.
instructions.5: Add enough chicken broth to the mixture and bring it back to a boil.
instructions.6: Add the vegetables and simmer on low heat until tender.

vl7-1.name: Vegetables (such as green beans or potatoes)

instructions.1: Prepare a cooking pot with water, salt, a whole onion, and vinegar.
instructions.2: Once boiling, add the vegetables and lower the heat until cooked through, then drain them in a colander.
instructions.3: Prepare a deep bowl with oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper, mixing them well, then add the vegetables to it.

instructions.1: Cut the green beans in half lengthwise, then chop them into small pieces and wash.
instructions.2: Blend the onion, tomatoes, bell pepper, and garlic with the salt and pepper in a blender.
instructions.3: Heat the oil in a cooking pot until warm, then pour in the blended mixture and bring to a boil over low heat.
instructions.4: Add the green beans to the mixture and sauté until they begin to wilt.
instructions.5: Pour in the broth and bring to a boil, then lower the heat and cover the pot, adding more broth whenever needed until the beans are cooked through.

instructions.1: Blend the onion, tomatoes, bell pepper, garlic, salt, and pepper in a blender.
instructions.2: Place the meat in a pot with oil and sear it, then pour the blended onion and tomato mixture over it until the tomatoes are cooked through.
instructions.3: Add enough water to cover the amount of green beans and bring to a boil, adding salt and pepper.
instructions.4: Once boiling, add the green beans and lower the heat until the vegetables and meat are fully cooked.

instructions.1: Heat the oil or butter well in a deep pan, add the frozen or fresh green beans, and reduce the heat while stirring continuously.
instructions.2: Add a little water, salt, pepper, and thyme, then cover and leave until the beans are cooked through.
instructions.3: Boil the rice in hot water, and just before it is fully cooked, drain it.
instructions.4: Finely dice the onion and sauté it in oil until golden.
instructions.5: Mix the sautéed onions with the cooked green beans, then combine with the rice; stir everything well and cover the pot to let it steam and stay hot after turning off the heat.

vl11-7.name: small onion juice, garlic, and sugar for the sauce
vl11-7.standardAmount: 1 onion, 2 cloves garlic, ½ tsp sugar

instructions.1: After peeling the green beans, soak them in water for half an hour, then pour out the water and repeat the soaking process once more, then drain thoroughly.
instructions.2: Prepare a pot by adding the oil, green beans, and the small grated onion over low heat, then add the vinegar, minced garlic, salt, and water.
instructions.3: Prepare the sauce by mixing small onion juice, 2 finely chopped garlic cloves, salt, pepper, cumin, and half a teaspoon of sugar, stirring the mixture well with a wooden spoon.
instructions.4: Once cooked, mix the green beans thoroughly with the sauce and place in the refrigerator for 3 hours.

instructions.1: Parboil the peas in boiling water until half-cooked, and boil the carrots separately.
instructions.2: Blend the onion, garlic, green pepper, tomatoes, and vinegar in a blender.
instructions.3: Heat the oil in a pot, pour in the blended mixture, and once it boils, pour in the broth and bring to a boil.
instructions.4: Add the parboiled peas and carrots, then leave on low heat until the sauce thickens and the flavors meld.

instructions.1: Sauté the peas and carrots in butter, then add about 2 cups of water or broth and leave on low heat until nearly cooked.
instructions.2: Fry a small minced onion in oil and pour it over the peas, then add enough broth or water to cover the rice, along with salt.
instructions.3: Add the rice to the peas and cook on low heat until tender.

instructions.1: Boil the peas in salted boiling water until tender, and boil the carrots separately.
instructions.2: Drain the vegetables in a colander, then sauté them in butter.
instructions.3: Prepare regular fluffy rice (see the Starches section).
instructions.4: Prepare the osag (see the Meats section).
instructions.5: To serve, prepare a deep bowl; place a layer of osag and pine nuts at the bottom, followed by a layer of carrots, then a layer of rice, and finally a layer of peas; repeat the layers (osag, carrots, rice, peas) and finish with a layer of osag on top.
instructions.6: Carefully toss the mixture in a serving dish.

instructions.1: Blend the onion, bell pepper, tomatoes, vinegar, and garlic in a blender.
instructions.2: Place the blended vegetable mixture in a cooking pot with oil or ghee and bring to a boil.
instructions.3: Add the broth seasoned with salt and pepper and bring to a boil.
instructions.4: Add the okra and reduce the heat until the okra is tender.

instructions.1: Heat the oil or ghee in a pot and sauté the minced onion, then the minced garlic, followed by the tomato juice or paste along with the salt, pepper, and vinegar.
instructions.2: Once the ingredients are well combined, add the raw cut meat or the minced meat and stir well, then add the okra and enough water to cover it.
